messages:
Kevin: Heads-up: saw a noisy-neighbor incident on Dedicated last night. Org-Delta had repeated short spikes, and Org-Epsilon's steady requests got smoothed down too aggressively. We should design per-org smoothing + burst controls that are fair across tenants.

Maria: I saw that too. The bursts were very short (lots of 20s spikes). Our current token-bucket + global clamp causes collateral damage to steady clients.

Jen: Are we prioritizing preserving legitimate short bursts (onboarding jobs, CI) or strictly protecting tail latency for everyone? That tradeoff will affect the math.

Kevin: Both matters. Primary goals: 1) prevent sustained QoS degradation for other orgs, 2) allow reasonable short bursts, 3) avoid credit gaming and churn.

Sam: Suggestion: dual-signal approach. Keep a token-bucket for instantaneous enforcement, plus an EWMA per-org that informs a longer-term refill rate. Add a short-window peak detector to block extreme microbursts.

Oliver: Implementation sketch: per-org token bucket + ewma_rate. Refill_rate = max(base_rps, ewma_rate * multiplier). Burst capacity = min(static_max_burst, base_burst + ewma_credit). Peak detector triggers if short_window_qps > threshold * ewma_rate.

Maria: Can someone post a simple config mock we can show product/ops?

Kevin: Pasted a quick YAML-ish mock (for discussion):

```
rate_limits:
  per_org:
    base_rps: 10
    max_burst_tokens: 300
    smoothing:
      method: ewma
      alpha: 0.2
      window_seconds: 300
    peak_detector:
      window_seconds: 30
      threshold_multiplier: 8
```

Jen: Two follow-ups: (a) recommended alpha/window tuning guidelines? (b) how do we support tiered overrides for enterprise orgs?

Oliver: Defaults: alpha=0.2 gives moderate memory (few minutes). Window=300s for EWMA. For enterprise we expose a tier_multiplier so refill_rate = base_rps * tier_multiplier (e.g., 2x for enterprise). Also allow explicit per-org base_rps.

Leah: Product asks that console show: (1) EWMA curve, (2) short-window peaks, (3) current credit balance, and (4) recent throttle events with reasons. Also want customers to request temporary burst increases via UI or API.

Sam: Telemetry items we need: raw_qps, ewma_qps, short_window_peak_qps, burst_tokens_used, credit_balance, throttle_events (tagged with reason: ewma_throttle | peak_gate | concurrency_limit), and tail_latency_pct90. Track percent of requests affected and latency delta pre/post throttle.

Jen: Alerting rules: if >5% orgs are experiencing ewma_throttle in a 15m window, tune is probably too tight. Also monitor top-10 org latency regression.

infra-bot: rate-limiter: created ticket RL-482 with runbook https://redwood.internal/ops/rl-482  assigned to @Oliver and @Maria.

Maria: I'll build a Grafana heatmap (per-org throttle status) and a problem list panel. Also adding a canary rollout flag (0% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%).

Kevin: Rollout plan approved. Must include automatic rollback if top-10 orgs see p90 latency increase >5% vs baseline.

Leah: Can we gate per-org smoothing overrides behind enterprise opt-in with audit logs? Product needs audit trail.

Sam: Yes. Feature-flag an admin UI + API for quota overrides. Emit audit events when a human or CI changes smoothing params. Also add a token scope for quota management.

Oliver: Implementation note: compute EWMA in serving plane for low-latency decisions, persist EWMA state to hot KV (sharded) to avoid cold-start anomalies. Periodic sync to control plane for observability. Keep enforcement local to reduce RPCs.

Maria: Action items:
- Oliver: prototype token-bucket + EWMA in serving runtime (PR by Thu EOD)
- Jen: define telemetry schema & dashboard wireframes (EOW)
- Sam: feature flag + rollout playbook + API changes
- Leah: console UX mockups for smoothing, credit balance, and override flow

Kevin: I'll open an RFC linking RL-482 and summarize goals. If anyone prefers a different smoothing stat (median-of-windows, percentile-based) say now; otherwise we'll start with EWMA and iterate after canary data.

Jen: EWMA is fine as a starting point. Re-evaluate with logged traces after canary.

Maria: ack :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: feature-flag created: ff/quota-ewma-2026, rollout_pct=0

Kevin: Thanks everyone. I'll draft RFC and attach telemetry & dashboard mockups once Jen and Maria have them.
